history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Roman Catholic parish church at Saligao, Bardez taluka, North Goa. Dedicated to Mae de Deus (Mother of God), it is widely described as the finest example of Neo-Gothic architecture in Goa, with whitewashed walls, pointed spires, buttresses and a belfry; attractively illuminated at night. Built partly from stones of the ruined Mae de Deus convent at Daujim (Old Goa), and holds the convent's miraculous gold-painted wooden statue of the Mother of God (possession ordered 20 June 1865), plus a black-stone Mae de Deus statue in the courtyard. Design credited to Goan architect Jeronimo Gomes under Portuguese/British influence. CSV STATE COLUMN ERROR: all five rows list towns under 'state'; this record is in GOA state.

town_description: Saligao is a large village in Bardez taluka, North Goa, a few kilometres east of Mapusa, set among coconut groves, rice fields and laterite hills. It is known for its Portuguese-era houses, the Saligao hill church landmark, and a long tradition of communal village institutions.

travel.airport: Dabolim International Airport (GOI), roughly 40 km south
travel.railway: Thivim railway station, roughly 10 km north-east
travel.road: On Chogm Road near Saligao; well connected by road from Mapusa (5-6 km) and Panaji (~20 km); local buses and taxis

visitor_information.best_time: November to February for pleasant weather; first Sunday of May for the Feast of Mae de Deus
